entries.text: Hi, I'm Mootrius!
This guide's purpose is twofold: to help me plan/document my own progress, as well as allow viewers to track their own progress if they choose to follow a similar path.

This is by no means as efficient a guide as, for example, BRUHsailer, but it does go into more detail than the Wiki's Ironman Guide. It follows a path I created to be a good combination of fun and efficiency. As such, you may find things that you would do differently — and that's fine! Feel free to deviate from it in any way you see fit, branching off however and whenever you'd like.

One thing you'll notice about this guide is that, due to the nature of chronologically reading it top-to-bottom, there are a lot of grinds that may come across as me saying "Do this from start to finish before doing anything else". I definitely think it's a good idea in general to break up your more active grinds with some AFK ones — and vice-versa. So, be sure to read a bit ahead before you start a section in order to find those things you can alternate between doing for your own sanity and to avoid burnout!
Hello from Mootrius!

If you're interested in a video format for the guide, you can find that here (https://www.youtube.com/ watch?v=BOgN7nAkOI8) (just be aware that the video version lacks the full detail that this Wiki version has).
If you have any questions at all, feel free to ask in my Discord server (https://discord.gg/mootrius)!
All in all, I hope you enjoy it!
— Mootrius

Right off of Tutorial Island, we're gonna get started with solving three things: money, prayer, and food. Doing so will provide us with an incredibly solid foundation for the rest of the account's progression.

We'll be focusing specifically on getting the Rogue's outfit and unlocking moonlight moth mixes and karambwans. More detail is provided below as to why we want these things so very much — and believe me when I say we do! Once you've gotten through this beginning section, you'll be very well set up for the quests, skilling, and PvM to come.
Our first goal is to solve the money problem — that problem being that money is necessary for buying things, and we don't have any yet!

The majority of our gold in the early game will be derived from thieving methods with the Rogue's outfit. There will be room here for both AFK and efficient methods, so you may choose which you'd like to do based on your preference and the amount of attention you have to pay (i.e. AFK methods during work, efficient methods during active playtime).
Getting the Rogue's Outfit
Bank everything from Tutorial Island upstairs in the Lumbridge Castle.
Pickpocket men until level 5 Thieving.
Steal from the Ardougne baker's stalls until level 25 Thieving.
Steal from Hosidius fruit stalls until 42.5 Thieving.
Complete the Stronghold of Security for 10k coins.
Buy a staff of air from Zaff's shop.
Buy mind, water, earth, and fire runes from Aubury.
Kill hill giants in the Edgeville Dungeon until 25 Magic (bank the big bones).
Complete The Feud, safespotting both bosses.
Blackjack until 50 Thieving.
Train Agility to 20 via the Draynor rooftop course.
Train Agility to 30 via the Al Kharid rooftop course.
Train Agility to 40 via the Varrock rooftop course.
Complete the Waterfall Quest.
Complete the Rune Mysteries quest.
Complete the Priest in Peril quest.
Train Agility to 50 via the Canifis rooftop course.
Get the Rogue's outfit from the Rogues' Den minigame.
Complete the Children of the Sun quest.
Do a combination of blackjacking and wealthy citizens until 60 Thieving.

Once you've completed the above steps, you'll be all set for money for the foreseeable future. Anytime you're low on money, either blackjack in Pollnivneach or pickpocket wealthy citizens in Civitas illa Fortis. This mix of Thieving activities should give you plenty of opportunity to make money either while AFKing or actively playing.

Next we'll want to solve the problem of needing prayer restoration. There are various combat training methods and quests that we'll want to be able to use the protection prayers during, so it's time to work on that!

We'll be working toward unlocking moonlight moth mixes via training our Hunter until level 75. This will be done primarily through hunter rumours, which give not only the Hunter training we need, but also a myriad of other rewards that are incredibly useful on an ironman account.

The main draw of these moonlight moth mixes is that they make us much less "ranarr-dependent" — meaning we won't have nearly as much need to focus an inordinate amount of our time on constantly getting seeds and herbs.
Unlocking Moonlight Moth Mixes
Buy/deposit 800 buckets of sand and 800 soda ash on the Catherby docks.
Train Crafting to 31 by making molten glass at the Edgeville furnace.
Train Woodcutting to 36 and Firemaking to 30 via Forestry.
Kill hill giants with Magic in the Edgeville Dungeon until you have ~200 big bones.
Complete The Restless Ghost.
Complete the Nature Spirit quest.
Complete the Lost City quest.
Buy some law and cosmic runes from Lundail at the Mage Arena bank.
Telegrab gold bars from the Varrock West Bank basement.
Buy some emeralds from the Ardougne Gem Stall shop.
Make some rings of dueling.
Use enough big bones at the Chaos Altar (running from Ferox Enclave) to get 30 prayer.
Complete the Fairytale I quest.
Complete enough of the Fairytale II quest to unlock the use of fairy rings.
Complete the Plague City quest.
Complete the Biohazard quest.
Complete the Ardougne Easy Diary.
Complete the Varrock Museum Natural History Quiz.
Train Hunter until level 46 however you like (some ideas here).
Train Hunter until level 75 via hunter rumours.
Complete the Twilight's Promise quest.
Use all of your blessed bone shards at the libation bowl at The Teomat.
Catch as many moonlight moths as you'd like to have moonlight moth mixes.

After the above steps have been completed, you should have at least 43 Prayer and the ability to catch moonlight moths. I'd recommend catching dashing kebbits for the hunter meat to make the mixes any time you run out in the future, as they're super easy to get to and fast to catch. For now, feel free to catch as many or as few moonlight moths as you want — what's important now is that you have solved Prayer!

Lastly for our solving of things, we're gonna be working on food. We can already pray against most damage with the Prayer solving we did in the last step, but now it's time to work on getting some hard food to eat.

Karambwans are an ironman's best friend when it comes to food, and for a few reasons. They're super easy to get, the Fishing method for them is incredibly AFK, and they're also a type of "fast food", meaning they have either a shorter or a nonexistent delay when you eat them. This allows you to get back to attacking faster after eating them. But for whatever reason you prefer, it's time to get going on getting them!
Unlocking Karambwans
Complete the Sea Slug quest.
Complete the Fishing Contest quest.
Buy and cook raw sardines from Gerrant until 20 Cooking.
Fish and cook salmon and trout at Barbarian Village until 35 Fishing.
Subdue Tempoross until 65 Fishing (solo preferred, mass okay).
Cook all of your raw fish from the reward pool.
Complete the Druidic Ritual quest.
Complete the Jungle Potion quest.
Kill ~50 skeletons near Tarn's Lair for two agility potions (2).
Complete the Tai Bwo Wannai Trio quest.
Catch at least a few thousand karambwanji.
Catch and cook a decent amount of karambwan.

Now, after having completed the previous steps, you can officially catch and cook karambwan! You'll be coming back to these for the rest of your account, due to how useful they are all the way into the late game, so get familiar with the DKP fairy ring! You can add the catching and cooking of karambwan to your AFK rota — especially if you got the fish barrel from Tempoross!

In this section, we'll be working on our combat stats via questing. There's a lot we'll do with combat going forward, so it'll be important to have a good baseline. This section will be composed of two subsections. The first subsection will focus on starting down the path of getting some solid melee stats, and the second will do the same but with ranged.

This section is a bit different from the last, in that it's not in a "checklist" style. This change is to help me be able to put more information regarding each quest/item with the table format. Instead, you can use the WikiSync functionality of the Wiki here for quests and/or click on the table item itself to "complete" quests.
These melee quests will kick off our combat training by helping us skip a lot of early training levels via the experience rewards they offer.

This section details the gear we'll want to assemble for our continued training, including information regarding how to get it. It will also include some training methods to actually get the stats necessary to buy/equip said gear. After everything is obtained, we'll train our combat stats to the following levels:
70 Attack 70 Strength
70 Defence
66 Ranged
75 Magic

There will be further quests and other activities in this section required to get this gear, and some of it will be bought with raw gp. The quests and activities are fairly straightforward, so just follow the order presented below — as for the purchases, I recommend going with either blackjacking or wealthy citizens to fund them.
IMPORTANT: Some of these items will require intermittent training before you'll be able to attain them. Be sure to read each subsection's preface to know when this is the case.
This subsection will include our first round of purchases to make from various shops around the game.
These purchases will help in our training for future gear unlocks, so they'll be important to get first thing here.
Below are the items to buy, their associated costs, and where to buy them:

Our first pieces of gear to go for are going to be the Fremennik helmets.

First we'll go for the regular helmets — the berserker helm, the archer helm, and the farseer helm — from the Fremennik Trials quest, and then we'll go for the neitiznot helm through the Fremennik Isles quest. We won't be able to wear the neitiznot helm until later when we get 55 Defence, so we'll hold onto it until then and just wear the berserker helm in the meantime.
Below is the rough list of steps to take to accomplish all of this:
Getting the Fremennik Helmets
Kill Borrokar for a lyre.
Complete the Fremennik Trials quest.
Complete the Daddy's Home miniquest.
Use your planks from Tempoross in your PoH to get 20 Construction.
Kill tree spirits in the Enchanted Valley with fire bolt to get a rune axe.
Cut willows in Seers' Village to get 56 Woodcutting.
Blow more of your molten glass in order to get 46 Crafting.
Complete the Fremennik Isles quest (put the experience rewards on Defence).
Buy your archer helm and farseer helm from Skulgrimen in Rellekka.
Next up we'll be going for the amulet of strength and the amulet of power. The former will serve as our amulet for melee, while the latter will be our ranged and mage amulet.

We'll be getting both of these amulets — in their un-enchanted forms — from the H.A.M. Storerooms, and then enchanting them when we have the appropriate magic level. If you've done wealthy citizens, you might have already gotten these two amulets.
While doing this activity, be sure to wear your Rogue's outfit for double keys. Here's a gear and inventory setup for you:
Next up we're gonna train a bit of magic — specifically until level 60. Doing so will allow us to subsequently unlock both the chaos gauntlets and a god cape.

We're gonna be doing this training via safespotting blue dragons in the Dragon Nest east of Tal Teklan. There's a super easy safespot to set up, the bank is very close nearby, and there's no 70 Agility requirement like in the Taverley Dungeon. It's really a great place to stock up on some dragon bones for eventual Prayer training — which is exactly why we're doing it!
So, using the below setup, go ahead and train your Magic to level 60 by water bolt-ing the blue dragons, banking all of the dragon bones in Tal Teklan.
Now it's time to get the chaos gauntlets and a god cape! These two items will be attained by completing the Family Crest quest and the Mage Arena I miniquest, respectively.
In order to complete the Family Crest quest though, we do have two requirements to get first — 40 Mining and 40 Smithing.
Below is a list of steps to get those requirements and complete the quest and miniquest:
Getting the Gauntlets and Cape
Mine iron ore at the Varrock East Mine until level 30 Mining.
Mine pay-dirt in the Motherlode Mine until level 40 Mining.
Pick up two iron bars from the Sunset Coast (hop worlds).
Kill goblins in Lumbridge until you get a chef's hat.
Enter the Cooking Guild and buy a redberry pie from Romily Weaklax.
Complete The Knight's Sword.
Complete the Sleeping Giants miniquest.
Buy iron and steel equipment from the Fortis Blacksmith and do Giants' Foundry until level 40 Smithing.
Complete the Family Crest quest.
Have Johnathon turn your steel gauntlets into chaos gauntlets.
Complete the Mage Arena I miniquest.
Collect your god cape from the sparkling pool.

This subsection has a bit of a choice for you to make as to how you'd like to go about training some melee stats. Our goal is to get 65 Attack and 65 Strength so that we can enter the Warriors' Guild to get the dragon defender.

The two main methods I'll recommend are Slayer and Scurrius. Either are very worth our time — the former for training the skill up and the latter for getting more comfortable with PvM. We're gonna wanna get 58 Slayer before too long for the Morytania Hard Diary, so I'd definitely recommend getting at least a bit of that done now, but if you wanna sprinkle in some Scurrius that's fine too!
For the Slayer training that you do end up doing for this subsection, here are a few guidelines to follow:

Use the highest Slayer master you can based on your combat level. Use Konar every 10th task for extra slayer points. Make some ruby harvest and black warlock mixes to use as you train. Use Magic and safespot instead for black demon and hellhound tasks.
Now, with our 65 Attack and 65 Strength, it's time to go for the dragon defender!

Your Defence level should be much lower than your Attack and Strength levels at this point. You'll need 60 Defence to be able to wield the dragon defender once you get it, so just be sure to kill the cyclopes with your dragon scimitar while training Defence until you get at least level 60 Defence.
If you're not familiar with how the defender grind works at the Warriors' Guild, it's gonna be pretty much as simple as this method that I recommend:
Steps
1. Kill some animated mithril armour for 200-300 tokens at a time.
2. Kill cyclopes upstairs for bronze through rune defenders.
3. Repeat Step 1 anytime you run out of tokens.
4. Kill cyclopes downstairs for the dragon defender.
Now, the last two things we need to do are train for and buy our remaining ranged and magic gear!
We're gonna be first training our Ranged to 60 and our Magic to 63, after which we can buy the mixed hide armour and mystic robes.
QUICK NOTE: At this point you should do the Ernest the Chicken and Animal Magnetism quests before you start training Ranged so that you can have an Ava's device while training.

Now we have three items that we're gonna get from the Mage Training Arena — Bones to Peaches, the rune pouch, and the infinity boots. Getting them will not only be good for the account going forward, but it will also help us train a decent bit of Magic throughout the process of getting them, getting us closer toward our goal of 75.
All in all, the three items will take a little while, but not that long in the grand scheme of things — especially considering the changes that were made to the Mage Training Arena in this update.

Below are the approximate amounts of runes (not including elemental runes for the Enchanting Chamber) that I'd recommend buying for the obtaining of these items. I'd recommend buying them from Lundail at the Mage Arena bank. You may have a few extra of each by the end if you buy these amounts, but that's good for future stuff!

If you're using the third-party client RuneLite, it's recommended to enable the Mage Training Arena plugin before starting this grind. This plugin improves the experience by providing helpful overlays and clearer visual cues for each room’s mechanics, making the minigame less tedious.

And now that we finally have all of our necessary combat gear, we're ready to train the rest of our stats to where we want them!
As a reminder, these are the levels we're going for:
70 Attack 70 Strength
70 Defence
66 Ranged
75 Magic

This subsection is pretty simple, as I'm just gonna tell you to train these stats by continuing whatever combination of the previous methods you prefer — Slayer, Scurrius, blue dragons, etc. The only specificity I'll make is that you'll want to be sure to have the following by the end of your training:
At least level 58 Slayer As many dragon bones as you can be bothered to have gotten
Other than that, do whatever you like!

Farming is an incredibly important skill on an ironman, so we don't wanna put it off any longer. Now that we have the Magic levels we just got in the last section, we can teleport around the map a lot more easily to do farm runs.

To start off, we're gonna quest our Farming level as high as we can, as to avoid the early levels of the skill, which are pretty painful. Then we'll start sourcing some seeds to plant — herb seeds in particular — and start planting them!

We've already got 17 Farming from completing the Fairytale I quest, but there are a few more quests we can do to boost our Farming level all the way to 35. This questing will save us from planting things like potatoes and onions, which are really slow and painful to level through. Instead, we can just do these quests and get a decent bit of the way into the skill without planting a single seed (except for those planted during the quests, of course).
Once we're finished questing, we'll move onto some proactive Farming in the form of the Tithe Farm! But for now, here are some quests for you to work on, in this particular order:

Now that we've got a decent start to our Farming level, we're gonna take it even further. We'll be spending some time at the Tithe Farm in order to get our Farming level to around 50. This will allow us to start planting some seeds we're gonna get in the next step, and also allow us to store enough reward points to unlock two things from the rewards shop: auto- weed and the herb sack. Auto-weed we'll enable right away so we only have to rake our farming patches one time ever, but the herb sack will have to wait until we get 58 Herblore in a future step in the guide (because you can't buy it without the Herblore level). For now we'll just not spend the 250 points for the herb sack.

I personally really like the 25x4 method, which involves doing 4 passes of 25 fruits each to get the multiple of 100 fruits that you need to get maximum points. This method can be a bit harder to get a hold on at first, especially if you're not used to tile-specific movement, but it offers great experience — and I personally think it's kinda fun!
Whichever method you choose (see here), go ahead and do Tithe Farm now until you have 300 points saved up!
Example of the 25x4 method tile markers.
Now that we've gotten through our lovely time at the Tithe Farm, it's time to get some seeds so we can actually start with our own farm runs.

Over the course of time we'll be getting tons of seeds from Slayer and other PvM, but for now we're gonna set ourselves up nice and pretty with some starter seeds from two main sources: master farmers and farming contracts. Master farmers are just a source of seeds via pickpocketing, which we're gonna work on for a little while now. Meanwhile, farming contracts are something we'll do now and (virtually) forever. They're just a great way to source seeds even far into the late-game of an ironman account, so we'll want to do them as often as we can be bothered to do them going forward.

The goal here is essentially to pickpocket master farmers in the Farming Guild for a few hours, doing farming contracts the whole time and going forward. I'll include a map link below of where the particular master farmer is that we'll be robbing.

Composting your plants (except for trees) can increase your Farming yield significantly. It also decreases the chance that your plants become diseased and die. If you're interested in just how much of a difference composting makes, feel free to read into it more here on the Farming page on the Wiki. There's a lot of math that goes into it, but the gist is this: compost = good.

The second-best kind of compost is supercompost, and luckily it's super easy to get. Here are the steps to getting some supercompost. Eventually we'll add volcanic ash to the mix for ultracompost, but for now supercompost will do just fine.
Steps
1. Buy some empty bucket packs from any farming shop.
2. Buy and deposit some pineapples from charter crewmembers into the nearby deposit box on the Catherby docks.
3. Put 30 pineapples into the big compost bin in the Farming Guild and close it.
4. Wait 90 minutes (coincidentally the same length of time as an herb run).
5. Empty the resultant supercompost into your empty buckets.
6. Congratulations! You have supercompost. Repeat the above steps as necessary.

The time has finally come! We have our Farming levels, we have our seeds, and we have our supercompost — so it's time to start with some actual farm runs. For now it's really only terribly important that we start with herb runs, but if you feel inclined to do more, then go right ahead! Later on, like after we get to Perilous Moons for example, we'll be swimming in tree seeds and will want to start doing other types of farm runs, and I'll include a section in the guide for when I recommend that specifically.
As far as which herb seeds to plant, I'd just recommend doing your highest tier of seeds that you can plant (that you have) and going down from there.

I'll include a table below with information about the herb patches that we've unlocked so far, so that you can get started. When we unlock new herb patches, or access to teleports that effectively unlock new herb patches, I'll include a note for you to start incorporating them into your herb runs.

In this section we'll be working on the hunters' sunlight crossbow. It will be a very powerful weapon for us to use for Ahrim at Barrows and even more going forward. It's just a really solid crossbow in general, specifically due to its attack speed and the decently high ranged strength bonus of the sunlight antler bolts we'll be firing with it. It's the primary reason we got 66 Ranged in the previous section of combat training.
This section will be composed of a few quests to do, as well as gathering some logs to eventually take to the Vale Totems minigame.

The main two obstacles to overcome for getting the Hunters' sunlight crossbow are 72 Hunter to hunt sunlight antelope and 74 Fletching to use its antlers to make both the crossbow and the bolts. Luckily, by following this guide, you already have 72+ Hunter — so
we just need to work on the 74 Fletching!

The method we'll be using to reach 74 Fletching will be Vale Totems. This minigame requires at least 20 Fletching, and we already do have some Fletching experience from The Fremennik Trials quest, so now it's time to get the rest (and then some to get us an even better head start).
Below is the list of quests to do:

From this point, we'll get the remainder of our Fletching experience from Vale Totems. However, we need to first gather the corresponding logs to use in the minigame itself. We'll be doing a bit of Forestry in order to get these logs, which in addition will allow us to get enough anima-infused bark to be able to buy the log basket from the Forestry Shop to aid us significantly while doing Vale Totems.
Here are a few things to note for this section:

You'll notice that I'm gonna be recommending you do maple logs all the way rather than yew logs. This is because yews just take way too long to cut without a much higher Woodcutting level and a dragon axe. Be sure to buy axe upgrades from Lunami's Axe Shop in Auburnvale as you go, up to the adamant axe. Then, when you hit level 41 Woodcutting, head on over to the Enchanted Valley to get yourself a rune axe from tree spirits (using fire bolt). Consider breaking up the grind here by alternating between woodcutting and Vale Totems as you go, just for sanity reasons.
The table below lists the amount of logs to cut and in which location. While gathering them, be sure to participate in every Forestry event that you see.

Now that you've got your logs, it's time for some actual Vale Totems! This is, in my opinion, a pretty fun minigame with a pretty fun gameplay loop. If you've never done Vale Totems before be sure to look up a supplementary guide, as while it's fairly simple, getting some information before will help the learning curve a lot.
Aside from just straight-up doing Vale Totems until 74 Fletching, there are a couple of things I would consider as you're going about doing it:

Rummage through your vale offerings every rotation or so, as getting the fletching knife as soon as possible will make this minigame go a lot faster. Sell all greenman masks and bow string spools you get at least until you get the fletching knife, as you can buy it from Ranulph with Vale Research Points. You can always come back for these two things if you really want them, or just keep any you get after getting the fletching knife. Don't use any of the Agility shortcuts and do step on all of the ent trails before getting the fletching knife — after you get it though, you're good to take things faster and just go for experience.
Next up is a real doozy of a step — getting the requirements for and completing the Morytania Hard Diary.

This grind is a pretty big one to do before Barrows, as it requires some fairly high stats and a decent few quests, but it will be incredibly worth it for both the extra runes from Barrows — 50% more, in fact — as well as a nice teleport to Barrows in the form of the Morytania legs 3.

The main two grinds here will be Agility and Prayer, as we need to get those to 71 and 70, respectively. Getting these two things done, however, will be very helpful for your account going forward. Higher level Agility, and therefore generally more run energy, is just useful all around while doing various activities. Piety will be similarly useful as it will quite drastically increase your Melee DPS when used.
Below is a table with all of the required levels for the Morytania Hard Diary, as well as how I recommend going about reaching them. Please note a few things about said table:

I won't be including the skills that you should already have by having completed earlier steps in this guide. I'll only include training method recommendations for levels past what you should already have from having completed earlier steps in this guide. I put the skills in a specific order based on later steps building off of levels gained from previous steps. As such, I'd recommend doing them in the order presented.
Display name Look up
Morytania Hard Diary Skill Requirements
Level Requirement Recommended Steps
Run the basic Colossal Wyrm Agility Course until 62 Agility.
Run the advanced Colossal Wyrm Agility Course until 71 Agility.
Complete The Dig Site.
Mine at the Motherlode Mine until 55 Mining.
Buy and use iron and steel items from the Fortis Blacksmith shop to use at Giants' Foundry until 50 Smithing.
Complete ~50 novice Mahogany Homes contracts to get 50 Construction.
Blow enough of your molten glass (from earlier in the guide) into the highest glass product you can to get 45 Crafting.
Cut and burn the highest level log you can burn until you have 50 Firemaking.
Use this calculator to determine how many dragon bones you need based on whether you prefer to use the Chaos Altar or the libation bowl for training.

The current ironman meta for Crafting is to gather up a ridiculous amount of giant seaweed and buckets of sand, cast the Lunar spell superglass make on them thousands of times, and then blow the resulting molten glass into various glass products. It's not super fun, but it's just the way things are, since other Crafting training methods don't even come close to the speed of this method.

Now to work on getting the broken zombie axe! Once fixed, which we'll do in the next subsection, this weapon is incredibly useful, as it bridges the gap between the dragon scimitar and the abyssal whip. We'll use it primarily for Perilous Moons in the immediate future, but it will be useful elsewhere as well.

There are two options for how to kill the armoured zombies that drop the zombie axe: magic or melee. Magic, which involves using burst spells on the Ancient spellbook, results in much faster kills than using our dragon scimitar with melee, but it does come at the cost of using a lot of chaos and death runes. Luckily, you (likely) have a lot of those from Barrows! If you got super spooned on getting tank gear from Barrows and didn't get as many runes, then you might need to use melee instead. Mage Setup
Melee Setup

For a mage setup, we're going to be using an ancient staff that we can buy from Eblis after the Desert Treasure I quest that we completed before. We'll also be wearing the tank gear we got from Barrows, because like the Barrows Brothers, the armoured zombies have essentially nonexistent Magic defence. If you're familiar with bursting/barraging (stacking enemies up by running rapidly between two tiles) then you'll know what to do — otherwise, look up a guide on YouTube to see how the technique is done. I recommend using smoke burst over ice burst for these armoured zombies, as using ice burst can make them get stuck on each other too much for the extra damage to be worth it. You'll also want to bring runes for blood burst, because although you'll be praying protect from melee to negate the damage from most of the armoured zombies, there are some that use Ranged and will damage you over time. Just cast the occasional blood burst manually when you need to regain some Hitpoints.
Tank gear from any melee Barrows Brother may be used.

Now that we have the broken zombie axe, it only makes sense to get it fixed so that we can actually use it! The way to do that is to get our Smithing to level 70, at which point we can just use it on an anvil with a hammer to repair it.

The method we'll use to get 70 Smithing is through Giants' Foundry. We already spent some time at this minigame a little while ago when we were working on the Morytania Hard Diary, and it's time to head back there now again for our zombie axe.

There are three reasons why we want to grind out the black mask right now. Firstly, we just want to have it (or rather eventually the slayer helm) for any Slayer training going forward. Secondly, the Shellbane Gryphon must be fought on a gryphon Slayer task, so it just makes sense to have it for the extra DPS. So, with all of those reasons being considered, it's time to go kill some cave horrors for a black mask! I'll include a gear and inventory setup below.

You don't need a witchwood icon as long as you pray melee the entire time you're in the Mos Le'Harmless Cave. The Shellbane Gryphon is definitely on the easier end of the bossing difficulty spectrum, but be sure to look up a guide if you haven't done it before. The main thing to consider is our gear setup, as the Shellbane Gryphon has a unique mechanic that deals a lot of avoidable damage to you if you weigh below 40kg specifically with your worn equipment, not including what's in your inventory.

Now, one very important point to make is that the Shellbane Gryphon can only be fought on a gryphon Slayer task. As such, you'll have to spend some quality time with Turael and/or Nieve. If you'd like, you can just use Nieve (after unlocking Wings Spread Slayer unlock) the whole way and complete each Slayer task until you get a gryphon Slayer task. Or, you can use a process called Turael Skipping to get one faster. For our use case here, this process involves getting a Slayer task with Nieve, and if it's not gryphons, getting a new, much faster Slayer task from Turael, cancelling the Slayer task from Nieve, and doing it all again until you get a gryphon Slayer task. I personally prefer the Turael Skipping method as it'll be much faster, but you can choose!
Either way, once you are ready to fight the Shellbane Gryphon, here's the gear and inventory setup I'd recommend:

The black mask weighs 10kg over the Slayer helm's 2.3kg, so we definitely want to wear it for weight. The tortugan shield must be worn during the fight to avoid a ton of unnecessary damage. The Dramen staff and Ardougne cloak 2 are for getting to the CJQ fairy ring, which is just south of the Shellbane Gryphon's Cave.

Once you get the Belle's folly (tarnished), you'll just need to take it on over to Giants' Foundry and use it on the polishing wheel, since you already have 70 Smithing from earlier when we needed to repair the broken zombie axe.

And now, after all the prep we've been doing for-seemingly-ever, the time has come to start the Perilous Moons! If you haven't already, complete the Perilous Moons quest — then it's time to get to actually grinding the bosses.

If you've never done Perilous Moons before, I'd definitely watch a guide to familiarize yourself with the content — but as usual, I'll include a gear and inventory setup for you to follow based on what we've collected in this guide.

Essentially, we're here until we finish the collection log for the Perilous Moons. Each set of gear from each Moon, including their weapons, is going to prove incredibly useful in our account's progression going forward.

The main thing to know about Perilous Moons is that there are three bosses: Eclipse Moon, Blue Moon, and Blood Moon, each of which is weak to one of the melee attack styles, being stab, crush, and slash respectively. As such, we'll want to use specific weapons while fighting them, which I'll detail in this subsection below.
In terms of gear and stats we're more than ready to fight the Perilous Moons, so let's get to it! Here's the recommended setup for each boss:

Tank gear from any melee Barrows Brother may be used.
As for strategy, here are a couple of notes for you:

You'll create the moonlight potions and fish and cook the bream in the dungeon. If you're having trouble with Blood Moon's healing, try learning the "step-under" method on YouTube. I recommend "target farming" the Perilous Moons, meaning that once you complete a set of armour from one Moon, stop killing it and focus on the remaining one or two.
Here is a resource for learning which directions to travel when either killing all Moons or target farming.
And well, there ya go! We'll be here until we finish the Collection log for Perilous Moons. It may take a while, but it'll be incredibly worth it for the uniques and general loot!

Now we're going to finish up all of the hard Achievement Diaries! Not only will doing so give us various benefits throughout the game (e.g. the Ardougne Hard Diary gives a 10% boost to pickpocketing everywhere in the game), but it will also give us something we love to see even more — antique lamps for Herblore experience!

Since we've got the Song of the Elves grind coming up in not too long, we need all the Herblore experience we can get. Hopefully you've been diligent in your herb runs, as having as many herbs as possible is gonna be really important in the next little while here — but if you haven't, get diligent!

There are a decent few skills we'll need to train to complete all of the hard Achievement Diaries, and we're gonna knock all of them out right now. We've been PvMing for a while now, so hopefully the change in scenery will be nice for you! Getting these skills up will also help prepare us for that Song of the Elves grind that I mentioned earlier.

Once you've started the quest, everything should go pretty smoothly. The part that will potentially give you some trouble will be the infamous Fragment of Seren fight.

I'll say, first of all, that if you end up really, really having problems with this fight, you could always go do Mastering Mixology until 77 Herblore and boost to 81 Herblore with a botanical pie to make Saradomin brews, making the fight a lot easier.
